name: Paula Tan
life: “I still remember measuring a badly placed rail while wearing a new suit.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Paula by a small Sunday habit. Paula checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I manage the building. The owner approved a handrail after I showed him how his own dad climbs.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a striped cotton shirt and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Paula has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Paula presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Paula keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Paula wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To secure a permanent accessible rail.
family: Ella Tran is Paula’s half-sibling. Paula can stop the walk at any corner. Ella chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Ella says, “I wrote WAIT FOR ME there when my brother was posted away.”
connections: Jules Wong. The building manager has to approve the rail the fitter can actually install.

reactions.situation: A relative offers to carry the patient up the stairs
reactions.response: Paula asks the patient whether being carried is an offer they want to take up.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Paula offers a little space from the crowd and waits for the player to indicate whether company is wanted.
